sections.heading: Overview
sections.body: The codebase in question is a legacy banking application, primarily developed using Visual Basic 6 (VB6). It is structured around a series of forms and reports, indicative of a desktop application designed for financial operations and customer management. The application relies heavily on event-driven programming, a common practice in VB6 applications, where user interactions trigger specific actions. This architecture suggests that the application was likely developed in the late 1990s or early 2000s, a period when VB6 was widely used for business applications due to its rapid development capabilities and ease of use.
cited_ids: Legacy desktop workflow implemented through VB6 forms and event-driven handlers

sections.heading: Architectural seams
sections.body: The architecture of the application is heavily reliant on forms and event-driven handlers, which are central to its operation. This reliance on VB6 forms creates a tightly coupled system where business logic is intertwined with the user interface. The use of ActiveX/COM components further complicates the architecture, as these components are integral to the runtime behavior of the application. This setup provides clear seams for modernization, particularly in decoupling the business logic from the UI and replacing or updating ActiveX/COM components to more modern equivalents.

sections.heading: Risk surface
sections.body: The primary risks associated with this codebase stem from its reliance on outdated technologies such as VB6 and ActiveX/COM components. These technologies are no longer supported, which poses significant security and maintainability challenges. Additionally, the application’s dependence on persistent storage backends and embedded SQL/data access logic suggests potential vulnerabilities in data handling and storage. The tightly coupled nature of the codebase, with business logic embedded in the UI, further increases the complexity of making changes without introducing errors.
cited_ids: Application appears to use persistent storage backends

sections.heading: Modernization implications
sections.body: Modernizing this application will require a strategic approach focused on decoupling the user interface from the business logic. This can be achieved by refactoring the code to separate concerns, potentially adopting a more modern architecture such as MVC (Model-View-Controller). Replacing ActiveX/COM components with modern libraries or services will be crucial to ensure compatibility with current operating systems. Additionally, migrating the data access logic to a more secure and maintainable framework will be necessary to mitigate risks associated with data handling. These efforts will not only improve the application's maintainability and security but also extend its operational lifespan.
